subject: P95/P99 performance check-in & POC scheduling for Acme.ai
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: P95/P99 performance check-in & POC scheduling for Acme.ai

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to align on your latency constraints and the higher-level success criteria. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Summary of what we heard from Acme:
- Target e2e p95: <= 180ms for single-turn chat generation (95th percentile across your production mix).
- Target e2e p99: <= 420ms for the same traffic profile.
- Sustained concurrency for your peak windows: 250 concurrent streams; occasional spikes to 500 for short bursts.
- Streaming requirements: token-level streaming with first-byte within 70ms of model start, and incremental tokens thereafter without >60ms inter-token stalls.

Redwood proposal (initial):
- Hosted API baseline: provisioned medium pool with streaming enabled, prefix caching, and dynamic batching tuned to your request size distribution. Expect p95 in the 120–200ms band depending on prompt length and model choice.
- Fallback plan: when hosted capacity saturates, route to quantized variant (same model family) with measured p99 uplift but lower cost.

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed):
1) Acme to confirm a representative 6-hour traffic window (timestamps + sample payload mix) so we can replay at our test harness.
2) Redwood to run a focused POC replay to produce p95/p99 E2E metrics for both "hosted" and your current vendor under matched concurrency. We propose Wed–Thu next week as a 48-hour window.
3) Exchange the attached latency matrix and SLO draft; please annotate any SLOs you need stricter than above.
4) Technical touchpoint: loop in your infra lead (Samir) to confirm networking and TLS settings for sustained concurrency tests.

Attachments: acme_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix to fill), redwood_slo_draft.pdf (proposed SLO language), poc_test_plan.csv (test harness fields).

I'll schedule the POC tentative window once I get the traffic sample and Samir's availability.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 performance check-in & POC scheduling for Acme.ai

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifying items before we commit to the 48-hour replay: 

1) The p95/p99 targets you listed match what we discussed, but note that our average prompt length is ~450 tokens (including system + user). Are your estimates above for 450-token sequences?
2) For streaming we need first-byte within 70ms only for short prompts (<200 tokens). For longer prompts, first-byte within 150ms is acceptable provided steady token emission after that.
3) Our current provider has a soft cap at 300 concurrent streaming sessions; the service degrades after that. We absolutely need Redwood to demonstrate stable p99 behavior at 500 spikes for at least one hour during the POC.

We'll attach the traffic window CSV by EOD. Samir — can you confirm network egress IPs and whether we should expect NAT or preserved source?

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, Acme.ai
elena@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 performance check-in & POC scheduling for Acme.ai

Thanks Elena — good clarifications. To address the prompt-length differences and the spike requirement, here is a narrow test plan we propose: 

POC test plan (high-level):
- Replay window: 2027-04-28 02:00 UTC -> 2027-04-30 02:00 UTC (48 hours).
- Workloads to run: baseline (450-token median, 10% > 1000 tokens), short-prompt subset (<200 tokens) for streaming-first-byte validation, and a dedicated spike test with 500 sustained concurrent streams for 60 minutes during off-peak replicating your spike pattern.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (client -> model -> client), first-byte latency for streams, inter-token stalls, token throughput, CPU/GPU utilization on the serving pool, and error/retry counts.
- Acceptance criteria: 
  * p95 <= 180ms for baseline workload 
  * p99 <= 420ms for baseline workload 
  * first-byte <= 70ms for short prompts; <=150ms for long prompts 
  * no more than 1% token emission stalls > 60ms during steady-state

Technical notes: we'll instrument the replay with our synthetic client (TLS handshake + keepalives) to mimic real connections. For NAT/IP, Samir — Redwood supports both preserved source and NATted egress; please let us know which you prefer for the test so we can confirm firewall rules.

I'll attach the updated SLO doc with the explicit acceptance criteria and the detailed test plan (poc_test_plan.csv) so you can review. Ben — can you confirm whether the hosted pool will run quantized variants concurrently during the spike window or only as fallback? That impacts throughput measurements.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_slo_draft.pdf (updated with acceptance criteria)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: P95/P99 performance check-in & POC scheduling for Acme.ai

Perfect — thanks for the confirmation, Elena. Quick operational notes and final asks before we lock the POC: 

- Benched configuration: hosted pool will start with non-quantized model variants for baseline runs. During the dedicated spike hour we will also enable a parallel quantized variant as a canary path (traffic-split 90/10) to observe degradation behavior and cold-fallback effects. We will not route production traffic to the quantized variant during your tests — it will be strictly observational.
- Please upload the representative 6-hour CSV and firewall IP list to the HubSpot deal (link below) by Tue 26 Apr COB so we can pre-stage test infra.
- DocuSign: attached a one-page POC statement of work; signing lets us provision the reserved test pool and guarantees priority scheduling.

Planned deliverables during the POC: raw latency traces (per-request), percentile summaries, GPU/CPU utilization, and an initial incident/playbook if we observe p99 violations during spike.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 (upload sample CSV)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/links/ACME-POC-2027

I'll pencil in the 48-hour window Mar 28–30 and send calendar invites once documents are uploaded and Samir confirms NAT behavior.

Thanks all — looking forward to proving hosted performance.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
